source_text: I. Quotiescumque servorum dei gloriosa facta memoramus, illi referimus gratiam qui et patientem tuetur in poena et victorem coronat in gloria. Martianus itaque consularis a Decio imperatore praefectus, Christianae legis inimicus, Achatium ad se iussit adduci, quem [secutum — sense: a follower and support; R reads Antiochiae regionis for illius religionis] quoddam ac refugium illius religionis audierat, et eo introducto ad se ait: Debes amare principes nostros, homo Romanis legibus vivens. respondit Achatius: Et cui magis cordi est vel a quo sic diligitur imperator, quemadmodum ab hominibus Christianis? assidua enim nobis est pro eo ac iugis oratio, ut prolixum aevum in hac luce conficiat ac iusta populos potestate moderetur et pacatum maxime imperii sui tempus accipiat; deinde pro salute militum et pro statu mundi et orbis. Martianus ait: Haec et ipse collaudo; sed ut obsequium tuum plenius imperator agnoscat, sacrificium illi solve nobiscum. Achatius dixit: Ego dominum meum, qui est verus et magnus, pro salute regis obtestor, sacrificium vero nec ille exigere, nec nos debemus exsolvere. quis enim homini sacra persoluat?
pass_a_gloss: Literal sense: Whenever we call to mind the glorious deeds of the servants of God, we ascribe favor to him who both protects the enduring one in punishment and crowns the conqueror in glory. Therefore Martianus, of consular rank, made prefect by Emperor Decius, hostile to the Christian law, ordered Achatius to be led to him, because he had heard he was a sort of follower and refuge of that belief, and with him brought in to himself he said: You ought to love our rulers, a man living under Roman laws. Achatius answered: And to whom is the emperor more at heart or by whom is he so loved as by Christian men? For unremitting and continual prayer is ours on his behalf, that he may complete a long lifetime in this light and may govern peoples with just power and may receive an especially peaceful time of his rule; then for the welfare of soldiers and for the condition of the world and globe. Martianus said: These things I myself also approve; but so that the emperor may more fully recognize your obedience, discharge sacrifice to him along with us. Achatius said: I invoke my Lord, who is true and great, on behalf of the welfare of the king, but sacrifice neither does he demand nor ought we to discharge. For who would pay sacred rites to a man?
pass_b_english: Whenever we recount the glorious acts of the servants of God, we render thanks to him who both upholds the sufferer under torment and crowns the conqueror in glory.

Martianus, then, a man of consular rank and appointed by the Emperor Decius, an enemy of the Christian law, commanded Achatius to be brought before him, since he had heard that Achatius was a kind of adherent and refuge of that faith, and once Achatius had been brought into his presence he said to him: You ought to love our rulers, as a man who lives under Roman laws.
Achatius replied: And to whom is the emperor dearer, or by whom is he loved as he is loved by Christians?

For we pray for him without ceasing and continually, that he may pass a long life in this light, and rule the peoples with just authority, and obtain an especially peaceful season for his empire, and thereafter we pray for the safety of the soldiers and for the condition of the world and the earthly orb.
Martianus said: This I also commend, but so that the emperor may recognize your loyalty more fully, offer sacrifice to him together with us.
Achatius said: I entreat my Lord, who is true and great, for the welfare of the king, but sacrifice neither does he demand nor ought we to perform.
For who would pay sacred honors to a man?

lemmas.gloss: pay in full, discharge a due

choices.term: patientem tuetur in poena et victorem coronat in gloria
choices.english: guards the sufferer in his punishment and crowns the victor in glory
choices.why: patientem and victorem are accusative singular masculine substantives referring to the same martyr at two stages, not abstract patience and victory.

choices.english: perform the sacrifice to him together with us
choices.why: solve here renders solvo in the judicial-religious sense of discharging a required rite, with nobiscum marking joint participation demanded by the prefect.

choices.english: for who would render holy offerings to a mere man
choices.why: dative homini marks the improper recipient and the subjunctive persoluat carries a rejecting rhetorical question, so homini is restrictive rather than neutral.
rejected: who pays rites to a man
